target_customer: Analysts and firms (especially financial) that need specific datasets, and aggregators who sell data
problem: Buying data was slow and costly; co-founder Matt Hodan said he spent 10,000 dollars in one year on data at a financial firm. Buyers posted free data requests and providers responded with priced datasets.
business_model: marketplace take rate (14 percent of each transaction from the provider)

founders.name: Matt Hodan
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2010-03-18) says the two founders were former investment bank analysts and that Hodan bought data at a financial firm. Bank names not given.

founders.name: Steve DeWald
founders.background_notes: YC page bio mentions fintech and software interests. Education and employers not listed.

competitors.name: Infochimps
competitors.what: Data set marketplace with a more collaborative, open data approach

technical_complexity.rationale: A request and listing marketplace with downloads in CSV and JSON and payments; no hard technology, per the YC and TechCrunch descriptions.

defensibility.rationale: Two-sided marketplace with a 14 percent fee and no proprietary data; Infochimps and Microsoft (DataMarket, October 2010) were building similar offerings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Infochimps bought the company in December 2010, reportedly in cash; the founders did not join and the site kept running standalone.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2010-03) cites a founder spending 10,000 dollars a year on data and datasets priced from about 5 dollars to several thousand dollars.

branding.name_origin: Descriptive name chosen for what the product is; no source states a story
branding.domain_note: A dataset lists datamarketplace.com as its website; the YC page links none.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and FlowingData in March 2010; nothing further found.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic descriptive name, easy to confuse with the many data marketplaces that followed, with no brand press beyond launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: Data Marketplace launched in March 2010 with a 14 percent take rate and was bought by competitor Infochimps in December 2010, nine months later, for undisclosed terms. The founders did not join, so this was a small exit of a young marketplace rather than an acquihire. Infochimps itself later moved away from the marketplace model, which suggests the category was hard.
notes: The 20K seed amount and investors rest on a single database (CB Insights, total raised over 3 rounds); the date 2010-03-02 comes from Seedtable, which gives no amount. YC lists status Inactive, consistent with absorption by Infochimps. A search snippet says Infochimps' marketplace round was 1.2 million (Nov 2010), not relevant to this company. Founders' count is two per YC and Altss; TechCrunch names only Hodan.
